question: Can an unsupervised objective decompose a transformer's representation into orthogonal multidimensional subspaces that align with mechanisms better than coordinate axes or one-dimensional sparse features?

key_findings.claim: Neighbor Distance Minimization learns an orthogonal partition by preserving nearby relations inside candidate subspaces while discouraging redundant partitions.
key_findings.evidence: The method optimizes a rotation and grouping of representation dimensions using local-neighbor distances, with split and merge operations that allow a feature to occupy more than one direction instead of forcing axis alignment.

key_findings.claim: On a GPT-2 Small circuit-oriented test suite, NDM concentrates several known signals into fewer subspaces than the tested unsupervised alternatives.
key_findings.evidence: Quantitative tests cover known positional, token, and circuit-related structures and report stronger concentration or selectivity for NDM configurations. Toy experiments verify recovery when ground-truth orthogonal structure is controlled.

key_findings.claim: Preimage inspection gives human-readable examples of what selected subspaces encode, but it is descriptive rather than a causal account of the model's computation.
key_findings.evidence: Nearest preimages for individual learned subspaces exhibit coherent token and context patterns. No intervention demonstrates that the complete mechanism is localized to those subspaces, and interpretation depends on sampled data and analyst judgment.

key_findings.claim: A Gemma-2 2B case study finds nontrivial routing between contextual and parametric knowledge, while the authors acknowledge coarse partitions and hyperparameter sensitivity.
key_findings.evidence: Learned subspaces differ in their association with prompt-context versus stored-answer behavior, demonstrating scale beyond GPT-2. The limitations section notes that discovered partitions can be overly broad and vary with neighborhood, partition, and dataset choices.

method.core_idea: Discover a non-axis-aligned orthogonal decomposition whose subspaces each capture a distinct local geometry of the activation distribution.
method.mechanism: NDM parameterizes an orthogonal transformation, evaluates neighbor-distance structure after projection into groups, and alternates continuous optimization with merge/split changes to the grouping. Resulting subspaces are scored on known signals and interpreted through their high-affinity activation preimages.
assumptions: Mechanistically meaningful features induce distinctive local-neighbor geometry in activation space.
An orthogonal direct-sum partition is an adequate model even when real mechanisms overlap.
The activation sample covers the concepts whose subspaces should be discovered.
Known GPT-2 circuits and behavioral labels are valid external checks without becoming training supervision.

techniques.role: Defines an unsupervised geometric objective for partition quality.
Allows features to occupy arbitrary multidimensional directions while retaining a complete decomposition.
Adapts subspace cardinality and dimensionality during learning.
Attaches qualitative semantic descriptions to learned subspaces.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic representations with known orthogonal latent factors.
evaluations.metric: Recovery/alignment of the learned partition with ground truth.
evaluations.result: NDM recovers the intended structure in the controlled examples across reported configurations.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small activations evaluated against a suite of known circuit and feature signals.
evaluations.metric: Concentration and selectivity scores across five principal tests.
evaluations.result: NDM produces the strongest or co-strongest aggregate concentration for several known signals, though performance varies by configuration.
evaluations.baseline: Coordinate partitions, random rotations, PCA-like controls, and compared unsupervised decompositions.

evaluations.setting: Gemma-2 2B factual-question prompts contrasting contextual with parametric knowledge.
evaluations.metric: Association of learned subspaces with the two information sources and qualitative preimages.
evaluations.result: Some subspaces show nontrivial differentiated routing, providing a scalable case study rather than a complete causal map.

limitations: The orthogonal partition assumption cannot naturally represent heavily overlapping or oblique mechanisms.
Subspaces are sometimes too coarse to yield a single stable human interpretation.
Results depend on neighborhood scale, partition hyperparameters, layer, and sampled corpus.
Most quantitative validation uses previously known GPT-2 structure; the Gemma case study is mainly descriptive.
failure_modes: Density or frequency artifacts may dominate neighbor geometry and appear as semantic subspaces.
Merge/split optimization can settle in a partition that combines unrelated mechanisms.
Nearest-preimage examples can invite cherry-picked labels without causal confirmation.
A mechanism distributed across overlapping subspaces may be fragmented or missed.
reusable_insights: Interpretability methods should permit multidimensional features rather than presuppose one direction per concept.
Local geometric preservation provides a label-free objective for decomposing activations.
Synthetic recovery, known-mechanism tests, and open-ended case studies form a useful three-level evaluation ladder.
open_questions: Can causal ablations establish whether learned subspaces are sufficient and necessary for the attributed computation?
How can overlapping subspace dictionaries replace the strict orthogonal partition without losing identifiability?
Do NDM partitions remain stable across corpora, checkpoints, and independently trained models?

competitive_landscape.title: Subspace-Aware Sparse Autoencoders for Effective Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Directly targets multidimensional feature groups rather than treating every interpretable feature as a single sparse direction.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its sparse-autoencoder formulation learns an overcomplete feature model; NDM instead partitions the whole representation into mutually orthogonal subspaces using local geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of Concepts: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Structure
competitive_landscape.relationship: Studies geometric relationships among sparse-autoencoder features and challenges an overly atomic view of concepts.
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes geometry after SAE feature learning, whereas NDM makes subspace geometry the unsupervised decomposition objective itself.

competitive_landscape.title: LEACE: Perfect Linear Concept Erasure in Closed Form
competitive_landscape.relationship: Treats concepts as linear subspaces and supplies a causal-style projection operation for removing them.
competitive_landscape.difference: LEACE needs a labeled concept and computes an erasure map; NDM is unsupervised and seeks a full partition before any concept labels are known.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: NDM is an unsupervised method for finding interpretable, non-basis-aligned, multidimensional subspaces in neural representations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It combines an orthogonal rotation, a local-neighbor objective, and adaptive group structure, then demonstrates both known-circuit concentration and a larger-model knowledge-routing case.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The full-partition local-geometry objective is distinct from sparse dictionaries and supervised concept subspaces; interpretability claims remain provisional without causal intervention or cross-run stability.
